subject: Data processor chain visibility & evidence bundle request
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@mediq.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: full processor chain visibility + evidence pack

Hi Priya,

We kicked off a security and privacy review ahead of our purchase order and need a clear mapping of Redwood's processor chain for any personal data Mediq will send to the API. Specifically: 
- Full list of downstream processors/subprocessors (name, role, country, nature of access)
- Any onward-transfer or cross-border flows and the legal mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, other)
- Encryption-in-transit and at-rest key flow (who holds keys, KMS/HSM provider)
- A short DPIA or memo summarizing risk mitigations for health data

Can you provide a single consolidated packet (CSV + diagrams + short memo) we can attach to our procurement file? We have an internal deadline of Tue 13 Apr — is that feasible?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Gomez
Senior Security Analyst, Mediq
elena.gomez@mediq.com
+1 415-555-0142

(Attachment: none)
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@mediq.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full processor chain visibility + evidence pack

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Looping in Karthik (compliance) so we can pull the roster and the DPIA summary.

We can assemble: a vendor roster CSV with roles and countries, an encryption key flow diagram, and a short DPIA memo. We should be able to deliver an initial packet by Mon 12 Apr EOD Pacific. Question: do you need formal signed amendments to the DPA for any listed subprocessors, or is a notice + roster sufficient at this stage for procurement?

Marking this as high priority — Karthik, can you confirm whether the KMS/HSM details can be shared in a redacted form for procurement (we typically provide provider + region + key custody model; we don't share raw key material).

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
(Attachment: none)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@mediq.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full processor chain visibility + evidence pack

Elena / Priya — quick note from Compliance: we can share the full roster and a DPIA summary. For KMS/HSM we will provide: provider name, region, key custody model (Redwood-managed keys with optional customer KMS for Private), and a schematic diagram of the encryption flow.

Two important procurement points: 
- If Mediq requires explicit subprocessor consent for any specific vendor on the roster, we'll need to escalate via legal for an amendment to the DPA — that typically takes 7–10 business days.
- For EU customer data we document SCCs where applicable; we will include the SCC reference and a link to our SCC annex.

I'm attaching the initial files we will push to Drive. Priya — suggest we send the Drive link to Elena and include a short readme and a CSV template mapping Mediq data classes to Redwood processing purposes.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Compliance
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
(Attachment stubs: redwood_vendor_roster_20270409.csv; dpia-summary-memo.pdf; encryption-key-flow-diagram.pdf)
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@mediq.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full processor chain visibility + evidence pack

Elena — sharing the packet we discussed: single Drive folder with CSV + diagrams + memo. Link and notes below.

Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/evidence/mediq-processor-chain
Readme (in folder): short_instructions.txt — includes mapping template and contact for follow-ups.

Attached files (in folder):
- redwood_vendor_roster_20270409.csv — includes vendor name, role (e.g., telemetry, logging, replication), country, access type, legal basis note.
- encryption-key-flow-diagram.pdf — shows Redwood-managed KMS in AWS (us-west-2) with optional customer KMS for Private deployments; indicates no raw key sharing.
- dpia-summary-memo.pdf — one-page DPIA summary describing data flows, retention controls, and mitigation for health data.

A few implementation notes: 
- If you identify a vendor that Mediq requires to be removed or that needs explicit consent, please flag the vendor name and we'll route to Legal for amendment — we can expedite for high-priority vendors.
- For procurement recordkeeping, the CSV has a column for DocuSign confirmation if a legal amendment is signed.

Please reply to confirm receipt and whether the packet meets your procurement checklist. Happy to schedule a 30-min sync with Karthik if you want to walk through any of the diagrams.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
